root_causes.description: product-catalog is burning 1-2 CPU cores (mean 0.952, max 2.149) while serving a very low request rate (~0.22 req/s), indicating injected CPU stress rather than organic load. The saturated CPU inflates response latency, driving p99 to the 10000ms ceiling and propagating to frontend and checkout which depend on it.

evidence.expected_baseline: sub-1 req/s throughput with CPU saturation confirms stress, not load-driven
p99 < 50ms for a leaf catalog read path

root_causes.description: Alternatively, a direct latency fault injected on product-catalog could pin p99 at the 10000ms ceiling. However the concurrent multi-core CPU spike favors CPU stress as the primary mechanism.
frontend and checkout show p99 at 10000ms purely as downstream propagation from the slow product-catalog dependency they both call; they are victims, not the origin.

remediation_steps: Confirm CPU stress on product-catalog by checking for a stress-ng / CPU-burn process inside the product-catalog pods.
Disable or reset the faulty flagd fault-injection flag targeting product-catalog (CPU stress) to restore normal CPU and latency.
If the fault is not injection-based, add CPU limits/requests and increase replicas for product-catalog to shed the CPU saturation.
Verify recovery by re-checking product-catalog p99 latency (<50ms) and CPU usage (<0.05 cores), then confirm frontend/checkout p99 returns to baseline.
Add alerting on product-catalog CPU saturation vs. request rate to distinguish stress from organic load.
